title: topology-img-core: a preregistered negative result on topological crossover and finite-size nonconvergence in task detectability
description:
A completed preregistered study relating the persistent homology of noisy images to task detectability, archived as a research record rather than as a manuscript. A fixed Gaussian lesion is embedded in a uniform field and degraded only by additive white Gaussian noise — no anatomy, no blur, no correlated noise, no reconstruction physics. Detectability comes from an ideal prewhitening observer; topology from a superlevel cubical filtration with H0 and H1 reported separately.

Result. A nonlinear topological crossover accompanies detectability loss and reproduces: for matrix 128 the H0 breakpoint recurred at sigma = 1.60 against an original 1.604, on independent seeds. Its location does not converge. Across matrix sizes 64, 96, 128, 192 and 256 the breakpoint moved and the breakpoint d-prime ranged from 3.32 to 7.75. The preregistered classification is Outcome 3, nonconvergence over the reachable range. There is no credible evidence for a critical phase transition or a universal detectability threshold.

The preregistration is verifiable rather than asserted. The freeze commit precedes the first data commit and continuous integration asserts that it is an ancestor of it, so the registered design cannot have been written after the data it governs.

No manuscript was written, and not because the result is negative. Outcome 3 was one of three results named before any data existed, so reaching it is an answer. The manuscript was set aside on scope: the object is a synthetic phantom rather than a medical image, no practice changes, and the readership is narrow. Publishing the record while declining to write a paper keeps the finding available and the reasoning open to disagreement. An exploratory extension onto real anatomical backgrounds was frozen and deliberately not executed, which the repository records explicitly.

No imaging data of any kind is used or redistributed: every image analysed is generated by the code in this archive.

notes: Archived as a negative research record, not as supplementary material to a manuscript. Freezing a study this way is legitimate only once its preregistered outcome has been assigned; stopping before that point looks the same from outside and is not the same thing. The concept DOI is deliberately not recorded as a top-level 'doi' field, which would tell Zenodo the DOI was assigned elsewhere and stop it versioning releases; record it as an isVersionOf relation once minted.
